key_insight: MEDIATOR converts clinical text into shared discrete tokens, improving EHR prediction across hospitals without manual ontology mappings.
clinical_relevance: Ontology-agnostic tokenization could help prediction models use more available EHR data when transferred between health systems.
method: Maps clinical concepts expressed as text into a shared vector-quantized codebook.
Learns from synonyms, enriched descriptions, code co-occurrence, and relation graphs.
Supplies the resulting tokens to an EHR Transformer.
evidence_signal: Across 20 MIMIC-III tasks and 14 zero-shot eICU tasks, mean AUPRC improved by 4.0 and 8.6 points over the strongest prior tokenizer, respectively; MEDIATOR used all eICU events versus 13% for a closed-vocabulary tokenizer.
watch_item: Results cover two EHR datasets; broader generalizability and prospective clinical utility remain unestablished.
paper_title: Discrete Neural Interlingua for Ontology-Agnostic EHR Modeling
